verdict.rationale: GitLab's own docs describe agents that autonomously turn issues into merge requests, remediate vulnerabilities, and review code while 'teams orchestrate from above the lifecycle while agents execute within it,' plus CI/CD automation for building/testing/deploying workflows — both point to background autonomous automation capability. However, evidence is entirely first-party marketing copy with no independent/hands-on confirmation of setup steps, scheduling controls, or real-world reliability of these agents running unattended. Missing for 10: independent verification of autonomous agent behavior, concrete setup/configuration docs for scheduled/triggered automations, and community confirmation these agents work reliably in background mode.
